biomarkers.name: BRAF V600E (papillary craniopharyngioma)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnostic hallmark of papillary craniopharyngioma and predictive of marked response to BRAF/MEK inhibition; dabrafenib + trametinib showed high activity in the Alliance A071601 study reported by Brastianos et al. (NEJM 2023), potentially reducing need for morbid surgery/RT

biomarkers.name: CTNNB1 (β-catenin) mutation (adamantinomatous)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Molecular hallmark of adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma; nuclear β-catenin helps distinguish adamantinomatous from papillary craniopharyngioma

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Epithelial tumour arising from remnants of Rathke's pouch; two distinct histologic subtypes with different biology
variants: adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma (more common in children but also occurs in adults; wet keratin, palisading squamous epithelium, stellate reticulum, cyst with 'machine oil' fluid, calcification)
papillary craniopharyngioma (almost exclusively adult; solid/papillary architecture, well-differentiated non-keratinizing squamous epithelium without wet keratin)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Benign histology but locally invasive; WHO grade 1

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Not well characterised; predominantly reactive inflammation around cyst contents, especially in adamantinomatous lesions
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Wet keratin nodules and calcification (adamantinomatous); fibrovascular cores and solid squamous nests/papillae (papillary)

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Rathke's pouch remnant epithelium / sellar-suprasellar epithelial remnants of oral ectoderm origin; both major subtypes are thought to arise within this lineage, with papillary lesions showing squamous epithelial differentiation
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Oral ectoderm (Rathke's pouch) during pituitary development
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Two distinct entities: adamantinomatous (often paediatric, resembles ameloblastoma/tooth enamel organ) with wet keratin, palisaded basal cells, stellate reticulum; papillary (adult, squamous papillary architecture, lacking wet keratin and stellate reticulum)
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Two distinct molecular pathways: adamantinomatous — CTNNB1 mutations activating Wnt/β-catenin; papillary — BRAF V600E activating MAPK
